title: Jambalaya
subtitle: Creole rice dish with chicken, sausage, and prawns
excerpt: A one-pot Creole rice dish cooked with chicken, andouille sausage, prawns, tomatoes, and the Holy Trinity of onion, celery, and pepper. Everything cooks in the same pot and the rice absorbs all the flavour.

recipe.sourceNotes: Jambalaya is a Creole and Cajun staple of Louisiana. It draws on Spanish paella and French influences, adapted through generations of Louisiana cooking. The Creole version includes tomatoes; the Cajun version typically does not.

recipeTools.notes: A large, heavy pot with a tight-fitting lid.

content.text: Jambalaya is a one-pot rice dish from Louisiana built on three proteins (chicken, smoked sausage, and prawns), the Creole Holy Trinity of onion, celery, and bell pepper, and long-grain rice that cooks directly in the seasoned cooking liquid. The rice soaks up the spiced, smoky flavour from the sausage and the chicken as it steams. The key is not to lift the lid while the rice cooks.
Heat the oil in a large dutch oven over a medium-high heat. Brown the chicken pieces for 3 minutes, then add the sausage slices and cook for another 2 minutes. Lift both out and set aside.
Add the onion, celery, and green pepper to the pot. Cook for 6 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and all the dried spices and herbs. Stir and cook for 1 minute.

Add the tinned tomatoes, stock, and rice. Stir to combine. Return the chicken and sausage to the pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer. Cover tightly and cook for 20 minutes. Do not lift the lid.
Lift the lid and push the prawns into the rice. Replace the lid and cook for a further 5 minutes until the prawns are pink and cooked through and the rice has absorbed all the liquid.
Taste for salt. Scatter over the spring onions and serve directly from the pot.
